info.title: Ontosyx API
info.description:
The Semantic Orchestrator — Knowledge Graph Lifecycle Platform.

## Response envelope

Every successful 2xx response is wrapped in:

```json
{ "data": <T>, "pagination": {"next_cursor": "..."}?, "meta": {...}? }
```

Each handler's `responses(... body = T)` documents the type of `data`, **not** the wire shape. Generated clients should either unwrap `data` in a post-processing step (the approach `web/src/lib/api/client.ts` takes — frontend callers receive `T` directly) or wrap every response type in the envelope shape when consuming the spec from a third-party codegen.

Error responses use a separate envelope: `{ "error": { "code": "...", "class": "client_error", "params": {...} } }` (see the `ErrorResponse` schema).

Revoke the caller's current platform JWT so it can no longer be
presented as proof of identity. Inserts a row in `revoked_jwts`
keyed by the token's `jti`, and drops the cached negative-result
in [`JwtRevocationCache`] so the next request from any holder of
the same token sees the revocation immediately.
post.description:
Idempotent — repeated calls are safe and return the same shape.
API-key principals short-circuit: API keys don't have a JWT
surface to revoke, so the endpoint surfaces a `400` so the client
can route them to the admin "delete API key" path instead.

`GET /api/evaluation/datasets` — list datasets in the active

post.summary:
`POST /api/evaluation/datasets` — upsert a dataset by
`(workspace_id, name)`. Re-importing under the same name
preserves `id` + `created_at` and updates `description` only;
every downstream FK (runs that referenced this id, items
keyed on this id) survives the re-import.

get.summary:
`GET /api/evaluation/datasets/{id}` — fetch a single dataset
header. Items live behind the sibling
`/api/evaluation/datasets/{id}/items` endpoint to keep this
path lightweight when the FE only needs the header.

delete.summary:
`DELETE /api/evaluation/datasets/{id}` — cascade-delete the
dataset + items. Runs that referenced the dataset stay alive
(`evaluation_runs.dataset_id` `SET NULL`).

get.summary:
`GET /api/evaluation/datasets/{id}/items` — list every frozen
`(input, expected)` pair in the dataset, ordered by
`item_key`.

put.summary:
`PUT /api/evaluation/datasets/{id}/items` — replace every
item under `dataset_id` with the supplied set in one
transaction. Items not in the request body are deleted; items
in both DB + request body are upserted on `(dataset_id,
item_key)`. Atomic — partial import never lands.

get.summary:
`GET /api/evaluation/runs/diff?baseline=<id>&candidate=<id>` —
per-axis delta + per-case row diff between two runs that
materialised from the same dataset. Returns a typed
`validation_error` 400 when the runs don't share a dataset
(the case_key correspondence the diff requires).

post.summary:
`POST /api/evaluation/runs/from-dataset` — materialise a fresh
run from a dataset. Atomic dataset-read + run-insert + bulk
case-insert in one transaction. Returns the created run plus
the case count for the FE response panel.

postconditions.description:
Rules evaluated *after* the action commits, inside the same
transaction — failure rolls back. Used for invariants that
depend on the post-state (e.g. account balance ≥ 0).

preconditions.description:
Rules evaluated *before* the action runs — failure aborts.
Typical uses: authorization, referential-integrity checks,
quota guards.

target.description:
Ontology target of the action. `ActionTarget::NodeType`
covers "create / update / delete a User", `ActionTarget::EdgeType`
covers "connect two existing objects".

drift.description:
Per-table drift between the stored fingerprint map and the
adapter's live fingerprint. Empty when there is nothing to
flag.

oneOf.description:
Cached `ox_source::AnalysisResult` shape verbatim — the UI can
render schema + profile + warnings without a second round-trip.

allOf.description:
Kind-specific body. The `kind` tag + the variant's fields
appear flat at this struct's top level via `serde(flatten)`.

AdapterDetail.description:
Detail view of one registered adapter.

Wire shape matches [`RegisterAdapterRequest`] exactly, except
`credential` is the redacted [`CredentialSource`] instead of
the raw [`Credential`]. This symmetry means admin clients can
render the GET result with the same form UI that drives POST —
only the credential field needs a "re-enter inline value"
affordance (since the raw inline bytes are not echoed).

AdapterDetailKind.description:
Per-kind detail body. Mirrors [`RegisterAdapterKind`] with
[`CredentialSource`] in place of [`Credential`].

`schema_name` appears on the variants that actually use it:
`Option<String>` on `Postgres` (defaults to `"public"` at build
time), required `String` on `Mysql`, absent on file-backed
adapters and feature-gated adapters that do not expose schemas.
The old flat `Option<String>` field on `AdapterDetail` is gone;
schema-less detail responses no longer carry a nullable
`schema_name: null` that meant nothing.

Adding a new adapter kind updates both this enum and
`RegisterAdapterKind`. The `From<&RegisterAdapterKind>`
conversion below uses an exhaustive `match` (no wildcard), so
forgetting the new arm surfaces as a compile error — the two
enums stay in lockstep.

supports_scan.description:
`true` when the adapter implements `DataSourceAdapter::scan`
— i.e. it can back federated link mappings (cross-source
joins via DataFusion). Adapters returning `false` are
introspection-only; mapping a federated link onto them is a
configuration mistake the admin UI should surface up-front
rather than discovering it at query time.

save.description: If true, persist the adopted ontology to database for use in Analyze mode.

AgentEventPayload.description:
Canonical persisted agent timeline payload. The stream adapter,
audit trail, and session reconstruction all use this shape so
replay does not depend on branchforge's private serde layout.

oneOf.description:
Scheduled task / reconciler. Used when no human principal
is in the loop (cache refresh cron, batch data-quality run).

AggregationRole.description:
Π-1: Analytical role of a property in a NL2SQL query — drives
whether the property appears in aggregation (`Measure`), group-by
(`Dimension`), carry-through projection (`Attribute`), or
identity (`Identifier`).

Industry reference:
- **dbt Semantic Layer** — `measure` / `dimension` / `entity`.
- **Cube.js** — `measures` / `dimensions`.
- **Looker LookML** — `measure` / `dimension`.
- **OMG SBVR** — noun-concept vs. verb-concept roles.

The `Identifier` variant maps to dbt's `entity` and is separate
from `Attribute` because LLMs treat identifiers very
differently (join keys vs. informational payload).

AmbiguityContext.description:
A column whose values cannot be interpreted from schema alone.

Persisted at source-analysis time; one row per
`(workspace_id, source_id, relation, column)`. Re-running analysis
replaces the row (same natural key), and `detection_source_hash`
invalidates stale resolutions that were attached to an earlier
schema shape.

clarification_prompt.description:
Human-readable question the admin / LLM sees. Authored once by
the detector; stable across re-runs so a resolution in flight
doesn't lose its prompt context when the hash rolls.

detection_source_hash.description:
Snapshot hash of the underlying schema + profile fingerprint
used at detection time. Any resolution whose
`context_source_hash` differs is treated as stale.

distinct_estimate.description:
Approximate distinct cardinality reported by the profiler —
`None` when the source adapter couldn't estimate.

nullable.description:
Did any sample row carry a NULL? Used by the resolver UI to
propose an implicit "missing" value mapping.

oneOf.description:
Repo-enrichment hint (ORM enum declaration, migration doc)
when the detector found a matching definition. Advisory only —
the admin must accept / edit / reject it when resolving.

sample_values.description:
Distinct-value samples pulled from the source profile.
Order-preserving, de-duplicated, capped at 20 entries.

history.description:
Resolution chain, newest first. The first row whose
`revoked_at` is null is the currently-active one; a fully
revoked chain leaves the context "unresolved".

AmbiguityKind.description:
Kind of ambiguity observed. Extending this enum is additive — no
existing `AmbiguityResolution` becomes invalid when a new variant
ships, because resolutions key off `context_id`, not `kind`.

oneOf.description:
Enumerate each raw value with a display + optional definition.
The right choice when the column's value set is narrow and the
admin doesn't want to promote it to a reusable CodeSystem.

Promote the column to an existing CodeSystem — the column's
raw values are codes within that system. Use this when the
values are already semantically managed elsewhere (e.g. an
ISO-standard status code or an internal coded-value table).

Pin a canonical concept on this source specifically — the right
move for `OverloadedName` where the same column name means
different things across sources.

AmbiguityMapping.description: The actual semantic binding the admin / agent chose.

AmbiguityResolution.description:
A resolved interpretation for an [`AmbiguityContext`]. At most one
resolution is active per context; creating a new one sets the old
one's `supersedes` pointer so the resolution chain is reviewable.

context_source_hash.description:
Hash of the context at resolution time. A later context whose
`detection_source_hash` diverges is considered stale and the
query planner will re-ask.

resolved_by_user_id.description:
User uuid when a human resolved it, or `None` when the agent
auto-resolved via an accepted repo hint.

revoked_at.description:
Soft-delete marker. Revoking without replacement returns the
context to "unresolved" state.

oneOf.description:
Previous resolution for this context, if any. Enables undo +
audit trail without deleting history.

The currently-active resolution, if any. Admins treat an
absent resolution as "needs attention".

AnalysisReportStatus.description: Health of the persisted analysis-report row.

AnalysisResult.description:
Result of a full source analysis: schema, profile, and any warnings
encountered during introspection or profiling.

Produced by [`IntrospectionKernel::analyze`]. Adapters themselves never
emit this directly — they expose atomic primitives and the kernel
orchestrates them into a full analysis, attaching warnings as
individual primitive calls succeed or fail.

AnalysisWarning.description:
Single warning emitted by an adapter or the kernel during
analysis.

The wire shape is **language-neutral**: backend never produces
user-facing prose. The FE renders a localised summary and hint by
looking up `class` in its i18n catalogue and interpolating
`params` (e.g. `params.partition_column`).

`detail` carries the raw provider error for an expand-on-demand
drilldown — operator/debug copy, not user copy. `group_key` is
server-computed (`class:scope.table` or `class:source`) so the FE
can collapse warnings sharing a fingerprint into a single card
without re-implementing the grouping rule.

detail.description:
Raw provider error text, English. Surfaces in the
expand-on-demand drilldown for operators; never the primary
user-facing copy.

params.description:
Interpolation arguments for the FE-side i18n message lookup
(e.g. `{"partition_column": "stdrd_ym"}`). Keys are stable
across FE locale switches; values are short identifiers, not
localised prose.

`selection` carries the user's intent through a single tagged
enum — `all` for a full sweep, `subset` for a standalone pick,

AnalyzeSelection.description: User-facing intent for a source analysis run.

ApprovalComment.description:
One entry in the comment thread attached to an approval request.
The reviewer's decision-time rationale is the first comment; any
pre-/post-decision discussion follows in the same thread.

approver_roles.description:
Workspace roles that may approve. At least one of these
must confirm before the action executes.

rationale.description: Human-readable rationale shown in the approval UI.

ApprovalPolicy.description:
Approval contract.

`Automatic` actions are executed without a prompt; `RequireApproval`
pauses the agent loop until a human confirms. Approvers are
declared by workspace role. A dangerous action (e.g. mass
`Delete`) should always require approval — the platform enforces
this by refusing to compile a tool manifest whose approval is
`Automatic` on a `Delete` target.

oneOf.description:
Apply immediately, no notification. For rollback + other
actions the system considers mechanical.

Apply immediately, broadcast a notification to the named
roles so stewards see the change in their feed.

Require approval, BUT skip the queue when any of the
predicates evaluate to `true`. The most expressive branch —
encodes "Admins sail through, high-scope edits get reviewed".
Always queue for approval.

ApprovalRouting.description:
Destination for a classified change. Variants are ordered from
most-permissive to least so a reader can eyeball routing posture
without a legend.

oneOf.description:
The author's role matches or outranks this reference. The
named-field shape (rather than a tuple `AuthorHasRole(RoleRef)`)
keeps the wire JSON readable and compatible with serde's
`tag = "kind"` internal-tag discipline.

The op declares a scope of matching `scope` with a value
strictly under `threshold`. Ops that don't declare the
matching scope do NOT fire this predicate — "no scope"
is treated distinctly from "zero-sized scope" so an op
that never tracks its magnitude can't auto-skip by
accident.

ApprovalSkipPredicate.description:
Predicates the `ApprovalRequiredUnless` branch evaluates. Every
predicate returns a boolean; the skip list is OR'd (first firing
predicate short-circuits to Apply).

The predicate set is intentionally minimal — only signals the
routing pipeline can evaluate WITHOUT executing the edit. That's
why `HasValidationPass` is absent: under the
`route → apply → validate → commit` pipeline, the validate step
runs AFTER routing, so at decision time no validation result
exists. Every matrix row that conceptually reads "role X with a
passing validation" collapses cleanly to "role X" — the commit
path still requires validate to succeed, so a bad IR never lands
even when the role gate waves it through.

oneOf.description:
Attempt produced a candidate that passed `Validate`. The
session may still continue (e.g. `Select` between two
successful candidates); this only describes the attempt,
not the session.

Validator rejected the candidate's IR shape (unknown
label, missing property, complexity guard tripped).

Runtime error during dry-run / execution (DB connection,
driver-side parse error, query timeout).
Attempt exceeded its time budget.

PromptBudget / token budget exhausted before the attempt
could complete.

AttemptOutcome.description:
Outcome of one attempt — the Refine fold reads this to build
the next try's ICL block.

affected_workspace_id.description:
Workspace impacted by the action. Differs from `workspace_id`
only for SYSTEM_BYPASS maintenance tasks that operate across
workspaces. When `None`, the affected workspace equals
`workspace_id` (the common case).

AuditRecord.description:
One record in the audit stream. The `provenance` payload is the
content-addressed PROV-O entity (`ProvenanceDef`) emitted at IR
commit time; the surrounding fields attribute it to the source
ontology so a multi-ontology workspace can render a rolled-up
view without an extra detail fetch.

AuditRecordPage.description:
Approval request — a queued gated operation awaiting review.
One entry in the comment thread attached to an approval. The
reviewer's decision-time rationale is the first comment; any
pre-/post-decision discussion follows in the same thread.
One record in the workspace-wide PROV-O audit stream. The
`provenance` payload is the content-addressed `ProvenanceDef`
emitted at IR commit time; the surrounding fields attribute it
to the source ontology.
Cursor-paginated audit page. The wire shape is
`{ items: [...], next_cursor?: string }`. `next_cursor` is
absent when no further pages exist.

Axis.description:
Six-axis labels, matching the Complete Map dashboard. Every
variant is a public wire contract — the FE filters / groups
edges by axis — so variants with no current emitter stay in the
enum rather than being removed; `#[allow(dead_code)]` is what
keeps that public surface honest without a linter nag.

AxisAggregate.description:
One axis aggregate for [`RunSummary`]. Per-axis mean across
every case scored on that axis. `count` is the denominator the
FE renders alongside the mean ("0.78 over 12 cases") so the
number isn't read in isolation — a 1.0 mean from one case is
not the same signal as a 0.78 mean from twelve.

description.description:
Optional free-form description. May be empty even when the
entity type normally carries one; the FE treats `""` as
"omit the description line".

id.description: Stable id string for the entity.

label.description:
Human-readable label. Falls back to `id` when no richer
text is available on the entity.

kind.description:
One of the kind strings the `/map-summary` endpoint emits —
`"node_types" | "edge_types" | "indexes" | "glossary_terms" |
"interfaces" | "code_systems" | "value_sets" |
"notation_patterns" | "concept_maps" | "value_range_sets" |
"rules" | "actions" | "functions" | "metrics" |
"object_mappings" | "link_mappings" | "provenances" |
"data_qualities" | "enrichments"`.

parallelism.description: Number of parallel batches (for large loads)

transactional.description: Whether to wrap each batch in a transaction

oneOf.description:
Primary or composite key column. Identity is its meaning;
no value-set / concept binding adds information.

`created_at` / `updated_at` / `deleted_at` and similar
audit timestamps. The timestamp itself is the meaning.

Free-form identifier whose value space is open by design
(UUIDs, opaque external ids, surrogate refs).

Operator-supplied reason for cases not covered above.
Surfaces verbatim in admin tooling — keep it short.

value.description:
Operator-supplied reason for cases not covered above.
Surfaces verbatim in admin tooling — keep it short.

BindingExemptReason.description:
Reason a property opts out of the "physical mapping must carry a
semantic binding" rule. Treating this as an enum (rather than a
boolean flag) forces authors to name the case so a future audit
can ask "is this exemption still valid?" without reading commit
history.

Most properties do not need an exemption — values that travel
without semantic meaning are the bug the binding rule is meant
to catch. The variants below cover the legitimate cases the
platform has identified; `Custom` is the open-ended escape for
schemes the catalogue has not yet promoted to a first-class
reason.

BindingKind.description: Which kind of query operation produced this binding.

oneOf.description: Canonical names are identical (case-insensitive).

The term's canonical name appears in the property's aliases,
or vice versa.
Number of term tokens present in the property's description.

Levenshtein-ratio-like token-prefix match between canonical
names, used when neither exact nor alias match fires. `ratio`
is in `[0.0, 1.0]`.

BindingSignal.description:
One signal that contributed to a candidate's score. Kept as a
tagged discriminated union so the UI can group / filter on
provenance — e.g. suppress alias-only matches behind a toggle.
Wire shape: `{ "kind": "<variant>", ...payload }`.

BindingStrength.description:
How strongly a binding constrains write-time behaviour and how
editors should rank the binding's domain when offering choices.

FHIR's binding-strength axis is the model: `Required`,
`Extensible`, `Preferred`, `Example`. We collapse FHIR's `Example`
into the same enum because consumers want a single dimension when
reasoning about UI ranking + validation policy.

decision.description:
`"approved"` or `"dismissed"`. Same enum the single-id
PATCH accepts; rejected with `invalid_enum_value` for
anything else.

ids.description:
Proposal ids to decide. Capped at 100 per call by the
`bulk_limit_exceeded` typed gate; clients split into
multiple calls when the cohort is larger.

reason.description:
Optional admin comment recorded against every transitioned
row. Surfaces in the audit log + each proposal's row
detail.

decided.description:
Count of rows that actually transitioned. Rows already in
a terminal state are silently skipped (same semantics as
the single-id PATCH), so `decided` may be less than
`ids.len()` when the cohort overlaps a previous decision
run — that's a normal "double-click safe" outcome, not an
error.

reviewed.description:
Count of rows that actually transitioned. Rows already in
a terminal state are silently skipped (matches single-id
semantics), so `reviewed` may be less than `ids.len()`
when the cohort overlaps a previous decision run — that's
a normal "double-click safe" outcome, not an error.

ids.description:
Context ids to revoke. Capped at 100 per call by the
`bulk_limit_exceeded` typed gate; clients split into
multiple calls when the cohort is larger.

revoked.description:
Count of contexts that actually transitioned. Contexts
without an active resolution are silently skipped (matches
single-id semantics), so `revoked` may be less than
`ids.len()` when the cohort overlaps already-revoked or
unresolved contexts.

errors.description:
Per-row errors. Empty when every row succeeded; a
non-empty list means partial success — the caller can
retry just the failed `case_key`s.

oneOf.description:
No cache participation — every query for this mapping routes
to the live source.

The planner may serve reads for this mapping from the graph
cache when the cache is fresh enough. `ttl_seconds` is the
freshness budget; beyond it the cache falls back to source.

schedule.description:
Optional cron-style schedule that invalidates / refreshes
the cache entry. Stored as free-form text and validated
at registration time; `None` means manual refresh only.

CacheHintKind.description:
Per-mapping hint for the graph-cache backend. The planner treats
`None` as "never cache"; `GraphCache` is an opt-in that names a
freshness window and an explicit refresh cadence.

Cardinality.description:
Edge multiplicity, expressed as one of the four canonical
shorthand variants. Each variant lowers to numeric `(min, max)`
bounds via the `source_*` / `target_*` accessors below — that
pair is what every consumer (SHACL emitter, cost estimator, FE
inspector) ultimately reads, so adding a fifth variant in a
future ADR is mechanical: extend the enum and add the matching
arm to the four accessors.

The shorthand stays the wire shape because it's how authors
think — "one to many" reads cleaner than `target_min=1,
target_max=u32::MAX`. When a deployment really needs a custom
multiplicity (e.g. "Order has between 1 and 5 line items"), the
SHACL `MinCount` / `MaxCount` rule on the property side is the
expressive surface; the edge cardinality stays shorthand.

ChangeRoutingRuleResponse.description:
Wire shape returned by the list / upsert endpoints. The
`change_type`, `routing`, and `risk_level` come straight off the
IR types — no parallel schema, the FE consumes the generated
`ChangeType` union alongside the rest of the matrix.

workspace_scoped.description:
`false` for global defaults, `true` for workspace overrides.
The UI uses this to badge override vs default rows.

ChangeType.description:
Taxonomy of edit operations the routing matrix knows about.
The variant set is closed — adding a new kind is a deliberate
schema extension, not a silent addition. Every `OntologyEditOp`
classifies into exactly one of these.

model_override.description: Override the LLM model for this request (e.g., "claude-opus-4-6").

oneOf.description: Bind this connection to a JWT principal + workspace.

Join a project room. The server responds with
[`ServerMessage::Presence`] (unicast snapshot) and broadcasts
[`ServerMessage::UserJoined`] to existing members.
Leave a room — releases every lock the caller holds in it.

Update cursor position. Throttled per
`collaboration.cursor_throttle_ms`; events inside the window
are silently dropped.

Request exclusive lock on an entity. Idempotent for the
caller — repeated acquires by the same user refresh the TTL.
Release a lock the caller holds. No-op for foreign locks.

ClientMessage.description:
Messages the client may send. The first frame after WS open MUST
be [`ClientMessage::Authenticate`]; anything else is rejected with
[`ErrorCode::AuthRequired`] and the socket closed.

CodeSystemDef.description:
A named, versioned set of codes that together carry semantic
meaning for one domain concept.

A `CodeSystemDef` is the terminology equivalent of a typed
enumeration. The `uri` field is how two systems with the same
short `name` stay distinguishable — "A" in
`urn:ox:order-status` and "A" in `urn:ox:customer-tier` are
distinct codes even though their `code` strings collide.

deprecated_at.description:
Deprecation timestamp for the whole system. A superseded
system still round-trips but the admin UI nudges users onto
`replaced_by_id`.

description.description:
Localized description — longer than `name`, used in admin UIs
and injected into LLM prompt context.

display_name.description: Localized display name shown in the admin UI.

hierarchical.description:
Whether codes form a hierarchy via
[`CodedValue::broader_id`]. `true` unlocks descendants-of /
narrower-than queries; `false` keeps the system flat
(catalogue shape). A code with `broader_id` set in a flat
system is a validation error.

kind.description:
Governance kind. [`CodeSystemKind::External`] systems must
not be edited through the admin UI — they are mirrors of an
authoritative registry and their codes must round-trip.

name.description:
Short human identifier (e.g. `"OrderStatus"`). Not required
to be Cypher-safe; this is display / lookup text only.

oneOf.description: Successor system when this one is deprecated.

uri.description:
URI that globally identifies the system. For internal systems
use `urn:ox:<tenant>:<name>`; for external systems point at
the authoritative registry (`http://unitsofmeasure.org`,
`urn:iso:std:iso:3166`, etc.). Optional — plain `name` is
enough for small deployments.

version.description:
Version string. Semver-ish but free-form — external systems
like ICD-10 have their own versioning scheme ("2019", "2024").

oneOf.description:
Tenant-editable business codes. Admin UI can add / remove /
rename entries. Typical for campaign codes, customer
segments, internal process states.

Immutable mirror of an external authoritative registry
(ISO, HL7, SNOMED, UCUM, internal legacy). The admin UI
treats codes as read-only; imports keep the local copy in
sync but never modify in-place.

source_ref.description:
Canonical source reference — URL, OID, or registry name
(`"http://unitsofmeasure.org"`, `"urn:iso:std:iso:3166"`,
`"urn:legacy-crm:cust-status"`).

CodedValue.description:
One code in a [`CodeSystemDef`]. Carries the raw `code` plus
localized display / definition + synonyms, hierarchy parent,
examples, and temporal validity.

aliases.description:
Alternate spellings / short codes / legacy synonyms used for
lookup. The admin UI index + LLM prompt expansion both read
this so a user query for `"ACT"` resolves to `"A"`.

oneOf.description:
Parent in the system's hierarchy — only meaningful when the
owning system has `hierarchical: true`. Validation rejects a
`broader_id` pointing into a different system and rejects
cycles.

code.description:
The canonical code (`"A"`, `"SPRING"`, `"KR"`, `"kg"`). Not
localized — codes are the invariant; display names vary by
locale. Case-sensitive; the admin is expected to pick a
consistent convention.

definition.description:
Localized definition — the precise meaning of the code.
Separate from `scope_note`, which carries usage guidance.

deprecated_at.description:
Deprecation marker — set when the code is soft-retired.
Admin UI grays out; new registrations rejected unless
`Severity::Warn` flag is acknowledged.

examples.description:
Curated representative examples (SKOS `skos:example`).
Distinct from the profiler-emitted `ColumnStats.sample_values`:
these are *authored*, not observed, so the LLM gets stable
anchors that do not drift as data changes.

oneOf.description:
Replacement code for deprecated entries. Runtime mappers
follow the chain transparently when consumers ask for a
deprecated code.

scope_note.description:
SKOS `skos:scopeNote` — when *should* this code be used,
what's the typical misuse to avoid. Longer than `definition`,
shown in the admin UI tooltip.

valid_from.description:
Start of the code's validity window. `None` means "since
inception". Used by temporal queries that need "what was
valid on 2024-01-01".

valid_to.description:
End of the code's validity window. `None` means "currently
valid". Distinct from `deprecated_at`: a code can be valid
but deprecated (still in use, new registrations discouraged)
or invalid (no new uses accepted at all).

CodedValueId.description:
Stable identifier for a [`CodedValue`]. Globally unique
inside an `OntologyIR` — two systems cannot share a code's
id even if they share its `code` string.

ColumnClarification.description: A domain clarification for a specific column.

ColumnLineage.description:
One output-column ↔ source-column attribution edge surfaced on
[`QueryProvenance`]. Authors of the federation planner pin one
of these per projected column whose origin can be statically
resolved (a direct `SELECT col FROM t` projection) so the admin
UI / downstream lineage tools never have to reverse-engineer the
scan-to-projection mapping from the rendered Cypher / SQL.

output_column.description: The result-set column the consumer sees.

source_column.description:
Physical column on the source side (table-qualified when
the source is multi-table; bare when the source is a single
inline payload like a CSV).

transform.description:
Optional textual transform applied on the way out (e.g.
`"UPPER(col)"`, `"concept_map(cs-2024 → cs-2026)"`). `None`
when the value is the source column verbatim.

ColumnProfileDef.description:
One column's distribution snapshot, taken from a specific source
at a specific time. Wraps the same [`ColumnStats`] the
introspection kernel produces, plus the location identity and the
sampling timestamp that locks the snapshot to a window.

column.description: Column name as the source advertises it.

relation.description: Source-side relation name (table / collection / file relation).

sampled_at.description:
Wall-clock timestamp of the sampling pass that produced this
snapshot. Used to age out stale profiles in admin UIs and to
attribute distribution diffs to a window.

source_id.description:
Source the profile was sampled from. Matches the `source_id`
used by the matching `ObjectMappingDef`.

stats.description:
The sampled distribution itself — null count, distinct count,
up-to-30 sample values, min / max. Carried verbatim so the
inference pipeline reads the same shape it always has.

ColumnProfileId.description:
Type-safe identifier for a column profile entry. Stable across
re-snapshots so the IR-level diff treats them as updates, not
add+remove pairs.

ColumnRef.description:
Qualified reference to a column within a source relation.

`relation` is the relation name (`public.customers`, a Mongo
collection, a CSV inline `records` relation). `column` is the
physical column name as it appears at the source — the adapter
layer applies any dialect quoting when it renders the scan plan.

ColumnSpec.description: A single column/field in the source data

has_nulls.description: Whether this column contains null values

name.description: Column name as it appears in the source

sample_values.description: Sample values (for LLM analysis / dry-run preview)

max_value.description: Largest observed value. Same redaction policy as `min_value`.

min_value.description:
Smallest observed value in the column. Suppressed when
`pii_redacted` is set so the bounds don't disclose
real-world ranges (date of birth, salary, etc.).

oneOf.description:
`Some(kind)` when a heuristic flagged the column name as
likely PII at collection time and the analyzer dropped raw
values to keep them out of `SourceProfile`. The user later
confirms or overrides through the admin UI's PII suggestion
flow; the confirmed `PiiKind` lives on `PropertyDef::pii_kind`,
independent of this collection-time hint.

sample_values.description:
Up to 30 distinct values. Empty when distinct count is too
high *or* when the column is flagged PII-suspect — raw values
are dropped at collection time so they never enter the
`SourceProfile` payload that downstream consumers (admin UI,
LLM context, audit log) eventually surface.

CommunityDetectionPolicy.description:
Detection policy — drives the offline cron that materialises
`CommunitySummary` rows the retrieval layer consumes.
Workspace-scoped per `(workspace_id, name)` UNIQUE.

Orthogonal to [`RetrievalProfile`] — a workspace can define
one detection policy and many retrieval profiles, or vice
versa. The eval surface fingerprints retrieval profile +
detection policy independently so an A/B over detection
algorithm doesn't perturb retrieval, and vice versa.
Workspace-scoped configuration for the Leiden community
detection cron (Microsoft GraphRAG canonical, Traag-Waltman-
van Eck 2019). The platform commits to Leiden as the
foundational community-detection algorithm; the policy carries
its tuning surface directly rather than indirecting through an
algorithm enum.

Operators upsert under `name = "default"` to override the
auto-seeded workspace row (Φ10.5); the bootstrap helper
[`Self::workspace_default`] returns the conservative defaults
new workspaces start with.

levels.description:
Hierarchical depth cap. Leiden recurses by aggregating
the refined partition into super-nodes; `levels` bounds
how deep the recursion goes. `1` means flat (single
modularity-optimised partition); the platform default is
3 (Microsoft GraphRAG convention).

min_cluster_size.description:
Smallest cluster the cron retains as a published summary.
Below this threshold the cluster is dropped from the
emitted set at every level.

resolution.description:
Modularity resolution γ. Higher → more, smaller
communities; lower → fewer, larger ones. Microsoft
GraphRAG ships 1.0; experiments tune within [0.5, 2.0].

seed.description:
RNG seed for the local-moving and refinement phases.
Two runs against the same ontology version with the same
seed return byte-identical partitions — the operator
trust contract.

CommunityDetectionPolicyId.description:
Stable identifier for a [`CommunityDetectionPolicy`].
Workspace-scoped per natural key `(workspace_id, name)`.

statements.description: Compiled load statements (parameterized — $batch must be bound at execution time)

query_ir.description: The lowered QueryIR, ready to execute via `/api/query/from-ir`.

status.description:
Terminal state — `succeeded`, `failed`, or `cancelled`. The
handler rejects `running` because a complete-call must
always pin a finished status. Wire shape is the snake_case
string (matches the storage enum's wire form).

acknowledge_quality_risks.description:
Must be set to true if the quality report has low confidence or high-severity gaps.
Prevents accidental promotion of low-quality ontologies.

ComplexityClass.description:
Complexity bucket pinned at promote time.

Closed enum — every variant maps to a distinct ICL inclusion
rule on the Brain side. Adding a class is one variant + one
arm in the Brain's exemplar-selection policy.

ConceptDef.description:
Workspace-canonical business concept — the identity layer above
any lexicalization the glossary records.

Implementer pin: graph types reference the primary `ConceptDef`
through `concept_id` and optional additional realizations through
`concept_realizations`. The canonical prefLabel lives on the
referenced `GlossaryTermDef` (via `canonical_term_id`); aliases fan
out across `alias_term_ids` so a multilingual deployment can ship
the Korean and English term records side-by-side without inventing
a second concept.

alias_term_ids.description:
Alternative lexicalizations — synonyms, abbreviations,
per-locale variants. Each entry resolves to a
`GlossaryTermDef.id` whose role is `Alias` for this concept.
Empty when the concept has no alias terms registered yet.

oneOf.description:
SKOS-aligned hierarchy parent. `Some(parent_id)` declares
this concept as a `skos:narrower` of `parent_id`; `None`
makes it a top-of-tree entry inside its workspace.

canonical_term_id.description:
The canonical prefLabel realisation. Points at a
`GlossaryTermDef.id` whose role is `Canonical` for this
concept. The GlossaryTerm itself owns the localised text.

category.description:
Author-supplied category (`"business_concept"`, `"measure"`,
`"dimension"`). Free-form; the platform never imposes a fixed
taxonomy here.

description.description:
Domain definition. Localised so a bilingual deployment ships
English + Korean text without duplicating the concept.

examples.description:
Illustrative examples that disambiguate abstract definitions
— sentence-shaped and locale-aware. SKOS `skos:example`.

governance.description:
Authorship and editorial trail. Mirrors the term's
`governance` shape so downstream consumers reach for the
same fields regardless of which entity they're inspecting.

id.description:
Stable identity. Survives prefLabel rewrites, locale flips,
and source-merge reconciliation. NodeType / EdgeType implementers
pin this id, not the term id, so lexical churn stays local.

lifecycle.description:
Lifecycle state. Drives UI affordances (deprecation
strikethrough, retired filter) and downstream resolvers
(NL-to-Cypher should route a deprecated concept through
its `replaced_by` automatically).

oneOf.description:
Optional executable spec for "what does it mean for a row
to belong to this concept?" — segment membership,
function-derived value, cross-entity predicate. The
realisation lives on the concept (not on each
lexicalization) so a translated alias term can never
declare a different membership rule.

Pointer to the successor concept when this one is deprecated.
Lets the resolver chain forward without touching individual
term records.

valid_from.description:
Inclusive lower bound on the concept's validity window.
`None` means "valid since the beginning of the ontology lineage".

valid_to.description:
Exclusive upper bound on the concept's validity window.
`None` means open-ended; a retired concept keeps `valid_to`
set so historical queries can still reference it as it was.

ConceptGovernance.description:
Editorial trail for a concept. Names the operator and the time
of the last edit so the audit dashboard can attribute a
definition rewrite without joining a side table.

author.description:
Stable subject of the human or system actor that authored
the concept. Matches `glossary` governance shape so audit
queries can union across both.

ConceptMapDef.description:
A declarative mapping between codes in two code systems.

Mappings are directional — `source_system_id` → `target_system_id`.
The reverse direction is authored as a separate `ConceptMapDef`
when needed; automatically inverting is unsafe when
[`Equivalence`] is anything other than `Equivalent`.

mappings.description:
The individual code-to-code mappings. Duplicates on
`source_code` are legal (a source code may map to multiple
target codes — record each with its own equivalence); the
translator returns all matches, the caller decides which to
take.

version.description:
Semver-ish version string — concept maps evolve as source /
target systems add or retire codes.

comment.description:
Optional author note explaining the mapping. Rendered in
the admin UI and surfaced via the translator when a
non-equivalent mapping is chosen, so the operator can see
why the codes are linked.

equivalence.description: Semantic relationship between source and target.

source_code.description: Raw code string in the source system (e.g., `"A"`).

target_code.description: Raw code string in the target system (e.g., `"ACTIVE"`).

ConfigHash.description:
Hexadecimal SHA-256 digest of canonical JSON over a typed
configuration block. Used by [`EvaluationFingerprint`] to fold
extensible decoding parameters (temperature, top_p, max_tokens,
system prompt prefix, …) into a single equality token; new
parameters extend the JSONB without forcing a column add.

oneOf.description: Both sides changed the entity's label.

Both sides changed the entity's description (default
localized text rendered for the diff).
Both sides changed the same edge's source endpoint.
Both sides changed the same edge's target endpoint.
Both sides changed the same edge's cardinality.
Both sides modified the same property in overlapping ways.

atoms.description:
One entry per atomic property axis (type / nullability
/ default / description) that both sides touched.

oneOf.description:
Draft modified a property that canonical removed (or
vice-versa) on the same entity.

Both sides added a property with the same name but
different content.

ConflictAxis.description:
One overlapping atomic axis on a Modify/Modify conflict.
Carries the canonical and draft values so the operator picks
without an extra fetch.

oneOf.description:
Inherited from the enclosing `RuleDef.kind`. Most constraints
use this.

ConstraintTarget.description:
The node / property / edge a constraint component targets. Most
components implicitly inherit the target of their enclosing
`RuleDef.kind`; constraints that span multiple targets (e.g.
`Disjoint`) name them explicitly.

id_token.description: The ID token from an OIDC provider

fingerprint.description:
Reproducibility pins for the run — committed ontology
version, dataset, model, prompt template, decoding config.
Required: a run that cannot answer "which configuration
produced these scores?" is uninterpretable, and the
platform refuses to author one.

metadata.description:
Free-form audit envelope (operator notes, run labels).
Reproducibility components live on `fingerprint`.

concept_anchors.description:
`ConceptId` strings. Distinct from `tags` (freeform
shorthand) so cross-team filtering by concept stays stable as
glossary wording and tag wording drift.

description.description:
Required on the wire — clients always send a `LocalizedText`
payload (`{default: ""}` is acceptable). Mirrors the canonical
`InsightDef.description: LocalizedText` shape; not making the
request DTO optional avoids producer/consumer asymmetry where
the response always carries the field.

oneOf.description:
Provenance the insight was originally computed against —
the platform's response basis at save time.

query_ir.description:
Logical query the insight executes. Validated as
`QueryIR` on submit so a malformed IR is rejected up-front.

allOf.description: Ontology draft origin: source analysis or base ontology.

CreateOntologyRequest.description:
Request body for `POST /api/ontology`.

`initial_operations` is optional — callers that only need the
shell (empty ontology with a pilot name) can omit it. When
present, the ops apply atomically: an error on any op or on the
post-batch `validate()` aborts the whole creation with nothing
persisted.

description.description:
Free-form description stored as the ontology's default
`LocalizedText`. Whitespace-only input collapses to the empty
localized text.

initial_operations.description:
Initial batch of edit operations applied atomically as v1.
Must contain at least one op — the handler rejects empty
batches with 400 so the endpoint stays symmetric with
`/edits`, which never accepts an empty operations list.

lineage_id.description:
Optional caller-supplied lineage id. When omitted a fresh
UUID seeds the lineage so cross-version references remain
stable across later refinements.

message.description:
Free-form commit message — surfaces in the version log next
to the first snapshot.

name.description:
Workspace-scoped name. Must be non-empty and unique within
the workspace (enforced by the store's `ontologies_ws_name_uq`
constraint).

CreateOntologyResponse.description:
Response body on successful creation. Carries enough data for
the FE to deep-link to the new ontology without a round-trip
refetch.

workspace_id.description:
When set, the prompt is a workspace-scoped override of the
global template. When `None`, it's a new global version.

parameters.description:
Free-form parameter map. The recipe runner reads keys per
algorithm; the API layer doesn't constrain the shape.

required_columns.description:
Column names the recipe needs from the source. Order is
preserved end-to-end.

ontology_lineage_id.description:
Ontology lineage this rule is scoped to. Required so two ontologies
in the same workspace that share a label name don't collapse each
other's rules.

fingerprint.description:
Reproducibility pins. `fingerprint.dataset_id` names the
dataset whose items are materialised into cases.

case_count.description:
Number of dataset items materialised into cases. Allows
the FE to surface "12 cases ready to execute" without a
follow-up `list_evaluation_cases` call.

name.description: Unique name within (user, ontology) — UI uses it as a handle.

pattern_ir.description:
The full PatternIR — nodes with positions, edges, filters, and
layout hints (zoom + pan). QueryIR is computed on demand from
`pattern_ir.compile()` and does not need to be stored.

oneOf.description:
Raw value stored directly in the data_sources config JSONB.
The admin accepts responsibility for the confidentiality of
the persisted bytes (use `SecretRef` for credentials).

Opaque reference to an external secret store. The string's
scheme (e.g. `env:`) selects the [`SecretResolver`] branch
that dereferences it.

Credential.description:
Either a raw value or an opaque reference to a secret store.

The `value` field carries the raw value on `Inline` and the
reference string on `SecretRef`. A `SecretRef` is resolved at
adapter-build time through a [`SecretResolver`]; the resolver
dispatches on the reference's scheme prefix (`env:`, future
`vault:` / `aws-sm:` / `gcp-sm:`).

`Arc<str>` storage: see crate doc-comment — makes the inline
100 MiB CSV / JSON case zero-copy from request body to adapter.

oneOf.description: A raw value is stored; the raw value is NOT returned.

A reference string — safe to echo. `Arc<str>` to match
[`Credential::SecretRef`]; the view is built by cloning the
Arc (refcount bump), not by duplicating bytes.

CredentialSource.description:
Redacted view of a [`Credential`] for GET responses.

`Inline` credentials have their raw value stripped and reported
as a single discriminator — the admin API never echoes an inline
secret back out. `SecretRef`s carry only a reference string, so
we do echo those (operators need to see which env var their
registration points at).

edge_kind.description:
Kind of relation — `"binds_to"`, `"maps"`, `"constrains"`,
etc. Future filters on the FE key on this value.

source_axis.description:
Axis that owns `source_id`. Drives node placement on the
FE grouped layout.

source_id.description:
Stable string id of the source entity. Compound ids like
`"node:Customer/tier"` point at a property inside its
owning node — the FE can split on `"/"` when it needs to
zoom past the node grouping.

source_kind.description:
Entity kind (`"property"`, `"node_type"`, etc.). The FE maps
this to an icon / label style independent of the axis.

items.description:
Persisted insight definition.

`query_ir` and `original_provenance` are stored as JSONB so the
persistence layer can round-trip historical payloads, but the
public wire contract is the canonical `QueryIR` /
`QueryProvenance` schema. Rust callers keep typed accessors via
[`InsightDef::query`] / [`InsightDef::provenance`].

author_id.description:
Author user id — owner of the insight; gates edit/delete in
the admin UI.

concept_anchors.description:
Concepts the insight realises. The wire payload is a
`Vec<String>` of `ConceptId`s — typed at the consumer
boundary so this crate does not depend on the full ontology
crate. The semantic axis: `tags` is freeform admin shorthand;
`concept_anchors` ties the insight to stable workspace
concepts, so cross-team filtering remains consistent even as
glossary wording and tags drift.

description.description:
Optional richer description / context — what the insight
reveals, why it matters. Localised.

expires_at.description:
When the insight stops being trustworthy. `None` = no
expiry. Useful for rolling KPIs that only matter for a
quarter; the dashboard hides expired insights from the
default surface.

oneOf.description:
Provenance the insight was originally computed against —
ontology id + version + registry hashes. Wire shape =
canonical `QueryProvenance` JSON.

query_ir.description:
The query the insight runs (logical IR — survives backend /
dialect changes). Wire shape = canonical `QueryIR` JSON.

question.description:
Human-readable question — surfaces as the card title in the
dashboard / inspector. Localised so a multi-region tenant
can serve the same insight in the viewer's language.

tags.description:
Open-ended tag set the admin UI uses for filtering. Common
values: `"trend"`, `"distribution"`, `"anomaly"`,
`"relationship"`, `"summary"`.

next_cursor.description: Pass this value as `cursor` in the next request. `None` means no more pages.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from a previous response's `next_cursor`

share_expires_at.description:
When the share token expires. `None` means never (legacy rows);
new shares always set this via `update_dashboard_share_token`.

oneOf.description:
Delegate to a pre-defined rule. The rule's outcome across
the population gives the score (pass / total).

Inline SQL assertion. Must evaluate to a scalar `float`
score in `[0, 1]`.

computation.description:
How the score is computed. Either a reference to a rule or an
inline source-dialect assertion the scheduler evaluates.

oneOf.description:
Most recent measurement, if any. Kept inline so a quick read
of the def tells the caller how the last run went without a
second round-trip to the measurement log.

threshold.description:
Score threshold in `[0, 1]`. A run whose score falls below
`threshold` marks the measure as failing; the consumer
(alert, dashboard, UI badge) decides what to do next.

DataQualityMeasurement.description: One run of a quality measure.

note.description:
Free-form note — useful for human reviewers when the score
drops and the dashboard wants to show the reason.

sample_size.description: Number of entities inspected, for context in the UI.

DataQualityTarget.description: What the measure is taken on.

oneOf.description: CSV file source

has_header.description: Whether the first row is a header

oneOf.description: JSON file source

root_path.description: JSONPath to the array of records (e.g. "$.data[*]")

oneOf.description: Relational database source (DDL-based)

decision.description:
`"approved"` or `"dismissed"`. `"pending"` is rejected —
there's no "un-decide" op; admins clear the row instead.

reason.description:
Optional admin comment. Surfaces in audit log + the
proposal's row detail.

query_ir.description: The QueryIR to reconstruct onto the canvas.

editable.description:
`true` iff the source QueryIR was a `Match` operation and
therefore fully representable on the canvas. `false` for
PathFind / Union / Chain / Aggregate / CallSubquery / Mutate /
Analytics — the UI should surface a "read-only" indicator.

pattern_ir.description:
The reconstructed PatternIR. Positions are always `None` — the
UI runs its own layout pass before rendering.

DependencyBucket.description:
One entry in either index of [`SchemaDependencyGraph`] — a target
(or source, depending on which index this bucket lives in) and
the edges that touch it. Tuple-shaped on the wire so the graph
round-trips through JSON cleanly (enum keys can't ride in JSON
object keys).

DependencyEdge.description:
A single half-edge of the dependency graph. Direction is implicit
in which index the bucket lives in:

- In an `inbound` bucket targeting *X*: `endpoint` is the entity
  that depends on *X* via `kind`.
- In an `outbound` bucket sourced at *X*: `endpoint` is the
  entity that *X* depends on via `kind`.

`kind` and `label` are identical between the two halves of a
single reference, so a consumer can correlate them by `(kind,
label)` if needed.

endpoint.description:
The other end of the reference — direction depends on which
index the enclosing bucket lives in.

label.description:
Short human-readable summary of *how* the two ends are
related — surfaced as a tooltip in the FE
(`"MinCount constraint"`, `"foreign-key bridge"`, etc.).

DependencyKind.description:
Classification of a [`DependencyEdge`]. Each kind carries a
distinct semantic — the FE picks an icon and groups by kind.

dry_run.description: If true, return DDL statements without executing them

executed.description: Whether the statements were actually executed

DesignGate.description:
One condition the operator must satisfy before designing.

`blocks_design` is the contract the HTTP layer enforces: any
`blocks_design = true` gate with `status = Unmet` rejects the
design call. `params` carries interpolation values for the FE
i18n catalogue (e.g. `pending_count`, `table_count`); the
backend never produces user-facing prose itself. `anchor` is the
FE element id to scroll to when the operator clicks the gate
row.

anchor.description:
FE element id for click-to-anchor scroll. `None` when the
gate has no inline control to focus.

DesignOptions.description:
Operator-confirmed inputs that override or supplement automatic
analysis. Submitted via `PATCH /api/ontology-drafts/:id/decisions` after
reviewing [`SourceAnalysisReport`].

confirmed_relationships.description: Implied relationships the operator confirmed as real FKs.

excluded_columns.description:
Source columns withheld from ontology design entirely. The
LLM never sees the column's metadata or sample values.

excluded_tables.description: Tables to exclude from ontology design.

large_schema_acknowledged.description:
Operator explicitly acknowledges designing against a schema
that exceeds [`LARGE_SCHEMA_GATE_THRESHOLD`].

partial_analysis_acknowledged.description:
Operator explicitly acknowledges proceeding with an incomplete
source analysis (analyzer warnings present).

pii_annotations.description:
PII annotations carried into ontology design. Each entry
flows into the resulting [`crate::ir::PropertyDef::pii_kind`]
and triggers redaction of sample values before they reach
the LLM.

DiagnosticLevel.description:
Wire-stable severity for [`QueryDiagnostic`]. Lowercase-serialised
so JSON clients can string-compare without knowing Rust enum
conventions.

DiagnosticMessage.description:
Structured diagnostic — `code` + English `message` + `params`.

See module docs for design rationale and wire shape.

code.description:
Stable dotted identifier (`<surface>.<phase>.<kind>`). Treat
the catalogue key set as a public API — renaming a code is
a breaking change for any consumer that has localised it.

message.description:
English human-readable rendering. Always present; serves as
the universal fallback for logs, alerts, and consumers
without a catalogue entry for `code`.

params.description:
Placeholder values for the catalogue template
(ICU MessageFormat). Keys match the ICU placeholders in the
localised template. `BTreeMap` for stable serialisation
order (deterministic logs, deterministic snapshot tests).

old.description:
Source node-type labels identify the endpoint entities, so we
carry them as `GraphLabel` for identifier validity; the label
is the user-visible artefact in diff reports rather than the
internal node id.

EdgeKind.description:
UML / OMG-aligned edge classification.

`Association` is the default for any plain semantic relationship
(Customer `PLACED_ORDER` Order). `Composition` and `Aggregation`
express part-whole relationships with different lifetime
semantics:

- **Composition** — strong ownership, the part's lifetime is bound
  to the whole. Deleting the whole cascades to the parts. Example:
  `Order COMPOSED_OF OrderItem` (an OrderItem cannot exist
  without its parent Order).
- **Aggregation** — loose containment, the part outlives the whole
  and is shared across wholes. No cascade delete. Example:
  `Department CONTAINS Employee` (an Employee outlives any one
  department; cross-department reassignment is normal).

The default is [`Association`](EdgeKind::Association) — both
existing edges and new authored ones get the safe non-cascading
semantics unless the operator explicitly opts into a stronger
classification.

oneOf.description:
Workspace-canonical concept this EdgeType realises. Mirrors
[`NodeTypeDef::concept_id`]; multiple EdgeTypes from
different sources can share a `concept_id` to declare
"these are the same business relationship". The reverse index
[`super::OntologyIR::concept_realised_by_edge_types`]
resolves a concept to its implementing edges in O(1).

concept_realizations.description:
Additional concepts this EdgeType realises beyond its primary
relationship concept.

display_name.description: Localized display name shown in the UI.

id.description: Stable UUID for this edge type.

oneOf.description: Logical inverse edge (e.g., PURCHASED ↔ PURCHASED_BY).

kind.description:
Relationship classification — UML / OMG-style. Drives
downstream affordances: cascade-delete inference for
[`EdgeKind::Composition`], hierarchical visualisation hints
for [`EdgeKind::Aggregation`], and a neutral default of
[`EdgeKind::Association`] for plain semantic links.

label.description:
Canonical, language-neutral relationship label (e.g. "PURCHASED",
"REVIEWED"). Used as the Neo4j relationship type. [`GraphLabel`]
enforces the `is_valid_graph_identifier` invariant at the type
level — an EdgeTypeDef cannot exist with a label that would
fail Cypher emission.

oneOf.description: Replacement edge when deprecated. See [`NodeTypeDef::replaced_by_id`].

source_role.description:
Role played by the source endpoint, e.g. "manager" for a MANAGES edge
from Employee to Employee. Distinguishes the *functional* role from
the edge label itself when the same relationship label could carry
different semantics depending on direction.

tags.description:
Free-form tags (e.g. "i18n", "derived", "temporal") for downstream
filtering and UI grouping. Not validated; ontology designer's choice.

target_role.description: Role played by the target endpoint (e.g. "direct_report").

EdgeTypeId.description: Type-safe identifier for edge types in an ontology.

dry_run.description: If true, returns generated commands without applying them.

user_request.description: Natural language description of the desired ontology change.

explanation.description: LLM explanation of what was changed and why.

oneOf.description: Updated project (null in dry_run mode).

EditOntologyRequest.description:
Admin edit request. `expected_version` is an optimistic-lock
guard — when the current ontology version doesn't match, the
handler returns 409 Conflict so the caller can refetch and retry.
Operations apply atomically: an error on any op rolls the whole
batch back.

dry_run.description:
When `true` the handler applies the operations to a **cloned**
IR, runs `OntologyIR::validate()`, and returns the resulting
[`OntologyEditPreCheck`] instead of committing a new version.
No audit row, no approval routing, no version bump. Useful for
"would this edit break anything?" previews in the admin UI.

message.description: Free-text commit message. Surfaces in audit log + lineage UI.

EditOntologyResponse.description:
Handler response — either a commit receipt or a dry-run
pre-check report. Serialised untagged so the JSON shape depends
on which variant the request carried (`dry_run=false` → receipt,
`dry_run=true` → pre-check).

OpenAPI exposes this as a free-form object; callers should
discriminate on the presence of `new_version_id` (commit) vs.
`classified_changes` (pre-check).

verified_by_name.description: Resolved user display name (from users JOIN). Not stored in DB.

Embedding.description:
Embedded representation of an operator question (or sub-
question from the translation pipeline). Carried as a typed
vector so the planner can pass it to per-engine vector-index
readers without round-tripping through a string.

Stored as a `Vec<f32>` rather than a fixed-size array because
embedding dimension is model-dependent (1536 for OpenAI's
`text-embedding-3-small`, 384 for `all-MiniLM-L6-v2`, 1024
for Cohere's `embed-multilingual-v3`); the platform stores
the source model alongside the vector so consumers know
which index to query against.

dim.description:
Vector dimension count, redundant with `vector.len()`
but cheaper to read in validators. The
`validate_dimension` test pins the consistency.

model_id.description:
Source model identifier (e.g. `"text-embedding-3-small"`,
`"all-MiniLM-L6-v2"`). Consumers route the vector to the
matching dimension's index — querying a 1536-dim vector
against a 384-dim index is a typed compile-time error.

vector.description:
Dense vector representation. Per-dimension `f32` is the
industry-standard precision for retrieval embeddings;
the storage cost scales linearly with dimension count
(1536 dims × 4 bytes = ~6KB per vector).

EndpointRef.description:
Resolvable reference to an endpoint of a link. Either `ObjectMappingId`
(the endpoint is already bound) or a bare `(source, relation,
columns)` tuple for endpoints that are mapped inline.

key_columns.description:
Column(s) whose values identify the endpoint instance. Must
match the endpoint object mapping's `primary_key_columns`
(validated at registration).

old_description.description:
Previous description resolved to plain text (pre-enrichment). `None`
when the property had no prior description.

apply.description: If true, save the enriched ontology. If false, preview only (dry run).

join_key_property_id.description:
Property on the target node used as the lookup key — e.g.
the IP address, the customer id, the postal code.

target_property_id.description: Property on the target node that receives the enriched value.

oneOf.description:
Free-form label for anything outside the typed set —
validation reports, exported documents, cached query
results, etc.

EntityRef.description:
What the record points at — intentionally a closed set of
ontology-modelled entities plus a generic free-form form for
subjects the core model does not type.

Equivalence.description:
Semantic relationship between a source and target code.
Mirrors HL7 FHIR `ConceptMapEquivalence`; same semantics as W3C
SKOS `*Match` predicates.

params.description: Interpolation parameters consumed by the frontend i18n catalog.

ErrorClassification.description:
Why a failure happened — sub-classification carried on the
`InferenceAttempt.outcome` enum. The classification routes
retry policy at the agent layer (e.g. `OutOfBudget` skips
`Refine` because retry cannot recover budget).

ErrorCode.description:
Stable identifier for collaboration error conditions. The FE
catalogue maps each variant to a localised message.

oneOf.description:
Side-by-side hybrid + trigram baseline retrieval over
the chosen surface. Each leg carries its own ranked list
alongside IR metrics; the FE dashboard pivots
`hybrid - trigram` per axis to surface where hybrid
actually moves the needle.

EvaluationActual.description: Observed outcome attached to an evaluation case after execution.

EvaluationCaptureAxis.description:
Axis tag for [`EvaluationMetricMetadata::Capture`] rows. One
`record_call` invocation lands one row per axis; splitting the
token axis into input / output / cached_input lets the operator
pivot per-axis without re-parsing a composite name.

EvaluationCase.description:
One (input, expected, actual) tuple inside a run. Mirrors the
`evaluation_cases` row.

case_key.description: Stable per-run identifier. UPSERT key alongside `run_id`.

oneOf.description:
Golden / reference outcome. Absent for unsupervised
evaluations.

latency_ms.description:
Wall-clock latency from invocation to completion. None
when the case has not yet run or threw before timing
could be measured.

metadata.description: Audit envelope stamped by the executor or sampler.

oneOf.description: Translate a natural-language question into `QueryIR`.
Free-form natural-language explanation / answer quality case.

Graph RAG anchor retrieval case over ontology navigation
entry points.

Hybrid-vs-baseline retrieval comparison. Same question
runs through both the hybrid (RRF 3-or-more ranker) path
and the trigram-only baseline against the chosen
retrieval surface; precision@k / recall@k / MRR / NDCG@k
land for each leg, plus per-axis lift on the
[`EvaluationActual::RetrievalComparison`] envelope.
Drives the dashboard chart that surfaces "where does
hybrid actually win?" without re-running the prompt.

EvaluationCaseInput.description:
Closed set of executable evaluation inputs. This is the
persisted case input and the dataset authoring surface, not just
an HTTP request DTO, so stored cases remain self-describing.

prompt_render_hash.description:
SHA-256 of the system + user prompt after template
interpolation. Replays the exact bytes that fed the
model for this case; the run-level fingerprint pins
the template id + version, this pins the rendered
output.

EvaluationCaseMetadata.description:
Case-level metadata. Kept closed because these envelopes drive
replay/audit UI, not arbitrary user annotations.

Per-case audit data is the *render hash* — the SHA-256 of the
fully-interpolated prompt body that fed the model for THIS case.
Run-level pins (prompt template id, template version, model id,
decoding config) live on [`EvaluationRun::fingerprint`] because
they're invariant across every case in the run; per-case Call
metadata only carries the dimension that actually varies per
case.

EvaluationDataset.description:
Frozen header for a reusable evaluation dataset. Mirrors the
`evaluation_datasets` row. Datasets are the unit of input
authoring — a curated collection of `(input, expected)`
pairs reused across runs (model A vs B regression diff, CI
golden gate, baseline pinning). The header carries no items
directly; items live in [`EvaluationDatasetItem`] keyed on
`dataset_id`.

name.description:
Workspace-unique identifier. The UPSERT-by-name flow on
dataset re-import collapses on this column.

EvaluationDatasetItem.description:
One frozen `(input, expected)` pair inside a dataset.
Mirrors the `evaluation_dataset_items` row.

oneOf.description: Reference outcome. `None` for unsupervised datasets.

input.description:
Prompt / context envelope. Mirrors `EvaluationCase.input`
shape so `create_run_from_dataset` is a straight copy.

item_key.description:
Stable per-dataset identifier. UPSERT key alongside
`dataset_id`; re-importing the dataset from CSV / JSON
replaces previous rows on this key.

metadata.description:
Free-form authoring metadata (tags, difficulty, locale, …).
Renders verbatim on the dataset detail panel.

EvaluationDatasetSummary.description:
Dataset header + per-row aggregate. The list endpoint
returns this shape rather than bare [`EvaluationDataset`] so
the FE can surface "12 items" inline next to each row
without an N+1 fetch. Headers stay separate from the
aggregate; the canonical [`EvaluationDataset`] shape is
unchanged for every other caller (get / upsert / delete).

item_count.description:
Total `evaluation_dataset_items` rows under this
dataset. `0` for freshly-declared headers; the FE
renders a muted-tone "Empty" pill when zero.

EvaluationDatasetSummaryPage.description:
Cursor-paginated evaluation dataset summary page. Mirrors the
frontend-facing page shape after the universal API envelope is
unwrapped.

EvaluationExpected.description: Golden/reference outcome attached to an evaluation case.

EvaluationFingerprint.description:
The typed bundle every evaluation run pins for reproducibility.

Every field except the explicitly-optional ones is required —
the whole point of the bundle is forcing the call site to
answer every reproducibility question at construction time.
`Option<T>` fields name dimensions that genuinely do not apply
for every run (e.g. deterministic retrieval-only scoring uses
no prompt template).

dataset_id.description:
Dataset every case derives from. Drives the case_key
correspondence two runs need to be diff-able. ON DELETE
RESTRICT — a referenced dataset cannot be removed while
runs depend on it.

oneOf.description:
Hash of decoding configuration (temperature / top_p /
max_tokens / system-prompt prefix / …). Folds extensible
per-call decoding state into a single equality token; new
dimensions extend the hashed JSONB without a schema change.

model_id.description:
Model that produced the candidate output. For deterministic
retrieval-only scoring (no LLM invocation), the operator
passes a sentinel id — the digest still pins the choice so
the run is comparable to itself across re-executions.

ontology_version_id.description:
Committed ontology version the run scored against. Pre-
canonical workspaces commit a draft before evaluating —
drafts cannot be evaluated as-is because the schema may
shift mid-run. The persistence layer enforces ON DELETE
RESTRICT so a snapshot referenced by a run cannot be
garbage-collected.

oneOf.description:
Prompt template id (`design_ontology`, `evaluation_judge`,
…). `None` for runs that do not invoke an LLM.

prompt_template_version.description:
Semver of the prompt template that ran. Pairs 1:1 with
`prompt_template_id` — both `Some` or both `None`.

oneOf.description:
Forward-compat slot. Φ10 lands the retrieval policy as a
first-class struct; the id is pinned here for runs from
that phase onward. `None` for Φ8/Φ9-era runs.

EvaluationFingerprintInput.description:
Pre-validation request shape for constructing an
[`EvaluationFingerprint`]. Carries raw decoding configuration as
free-form JSON; the canonicaliser hashes it on the way through.
This is the wire shape an HTTP / cron / sampler caller submits;
the canonical [`EvaluationFingerprint`] only escapes from
`into_fingerprint`.

decoding_config.description:
Free-form decoding configuration — the canonicaliser hashes
it into [`EvaluationFingerprint::decoding_config_hash`]. Two
inputs that differ only in JSON key ordering hash
identically; per-call deterministic replay relies on this.

EvaluationMetric.description:
One score on one rubric axis for one case. Mirrors the
`evaluation_metrics` row.

name.description:
Free-form rubric name. RAGAS canonicals
(`faithfulness`, `answer_relevance`, `context_precision`,
`context_recall`) plus tenant-defined names.

provenance_id.description:
PROV-O activity that produced this score. `Some` for
LLM-judged rows (RAGAS / safety judge); `None` for
capture-axis observations (latency / tokens / cost) whose
provenance is attached to the underlying case via
[`EvaluationCaseMetadata::Call`]. `ON DELETE RESTRICT` —
the audit trail outlives the metric.

reasoning.description:
Optional natural-language reasoning emitted by an LLM
judge. Absent for code-side rubrics.

score.description:
Normalised to `[0.0, 1.0]`. Validation is the caller's
concern — the storage layer keeps the column unbounded so
rubrics with a different domain (latency p95 ms,
hallucination count) can ride on the same column without
a forced rescale.

EvaluationMetricMetadata.description:
Metric-level provenance. The enum is intentionally finite so
dashboards can group and filter metric rows without probing
arbitrary JSON keys.

EvaluationRetrievedAnchor.description: One ranked retrieval hit captured on a graph-RAG evaluation case.

EvaluationRun.description:
One evaluation batch. Mirrors the `evaluation_runs` row.

Reproducibility components (ontology version, dataset, model,
prompt template, decoding config, retrieval profile) live in
[`EvaluationFingerprint`] — the typed bundle every run pins at
construction. The legacy nullable `ontology_version_id` /
`dataset_id` columns are gone: a run that cannot answer the
question "which ontology version did I score against?" is
uninterpretable, and the platform refuses to author one.

fingerprint.description:
Typed reproducibility bundle. Persisted as
`evaluation_runs.fingerprint_components JSONB NOT NULL`;
the digest below carries the equality token for fast
"same configuration" lookups.

fingerprint_digest.description:
SHA-256 of [`EvaluationFingerprint::digest`], persisted as
`evaluation_runs.fingerprint_digest VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL`.
Two runs are configured identically iff their digests match.

metadata.description:
Free-form audit envelope. Reproducibility components live
on [`Self::fingerprint`] — operator notes, run labels, and
other non-configuration tags ride here.

EvaluationRunPage.description:
Cursor-paginated evaluation run page. The runtime envelope is
`ApiResponse::page`, which the FE client unwraps to this shape.

EvaluationRunStatus.description:
Status of an [`EvaluationRun`]. Wire shape is the
snake_case string ("running" / "succeeded" / …) so adding
a future variant is a Rust-side change with no migration;
the catalog parity test pins the string set.

ExcludedColumn.description:
Source column the operator wants withheld from ontology design
entirely. The column's metadata and sample values never reach
the LLM, and the resulting ontology contains no
[`crate::ir::PropertyDef`] for it.

ontology_id.description:
Optional saved-ontology id. When present, the OntologyValidator
gates the compiled Cypher against this ontology so a canvas built
on a stale schema gets rejected with a precise "unknown label"
error instead of a generic driver failure.

query_ir.description: The QueryIR to compile and execute.

compiled_query.description: The compiled query statement in the target language.

oneOf.description: Widget hint for optimal result visualization.

data.description: Data batches to load. Each element is a JSON object representing one record.

ontology.description: OntologyIR for the target graph schema.

oneOf.description: Optional pre-computed load plan. If omitted, the plan is generated via LLM.

connection_string.description: Source database connection string (required for fetching data)

plan.description: Pre-computed load plan (from generate_load_plan or manual)

ontology_id.description:
Optional saved-ontology id. When present, the runtime's
OntologyValidator gates the query against this ontology (rejects
unknown labels / relationship types / property keys). When
omitted, the raw path stays ontology-free and only the safety
+ workspace-scope gates apply.

query.description: Raw query statement in the target language (e.g., Cypher).

oneOf.description: Query result rows and metadata.

element_id.description: Graph element ID of the node to expand.

limit.description: Max neighbors to return (default 50, capped at 200).

ExpandNeighbor.description: A neighbor of an expanded node.

oneOf.description: A literal value

A named parameter placeholder: `$name` in Cypher.

Used for caller-supplied values that vary across executions of the
same compiled query — the query plan stays warm in the driver's
cache, and only the parameter values change per run. Compiles to
a `$name` reference without entering the auto-generated parameter
table, so the caller must bind the value at execution time (Neo4j
fails loud with a missing-parameter error if not).

The compiler rejects a name that doesn't match
`is_valid_graph_identifier` to prevent Cypher injection via the
parameter surface. Distinct from `Literal` (inline value baked
into the plan) and from the compiler's internal `$p0` / `$p1`
autogenerated params (opaque — caller can't change them).
A property reference: variable.field (field is None when referencing the whole variable)
Binary comparison: left op right
Logical combination: left AND/OR right
Negation: NOT expr
IN check: expr IN [values]
NULL check: expr IS NULL / IS NOT NULL
String operations: STARTS WITH, ENDS WITH, CONTAINS
Function call: function(args)
Pattern existence check: EXISTS { (a)-[:KNOWS]->(b) }
CASE expression: simple or searched
ELSE result (defaults to null if omitted)
Optional operand for simple CASE (CASE expr WHEN ...)

Subquery expression — evaluates a nested query and returns scalar/list result.
Compiles to Cypher COUNT { ... } or CALL { ... } depending on context.

import_variables.description: Variables from outer scope to import into subquery

selection.description:
Which tables of the new source to introspect. Required —
`kind: "all"` to take everything advertised, `kind: "subset"`
for a curated list, `kind: "extend"` to grow the existing
baseline with the named tables.

source.description: New data source to merge into the project.

reconcile_report.description: Report on ID reconciliation between existing and new ontology entities.

oneOf.description:

Another Ontosyx workspace / ontology — joins are evaluated

Pointer to the external service.

`kind` is a small, closed set so the planner can refuse a config

hint.description: Description or domain hint (e.g., "ISO 4217 currency code", "Unix timestamp in ms")

inferred.description:
True if this relationship was inferred from document structure (e.g., JSON nesting)
rather than declared in the source schema (e.g., DB foreign key constraint).

edge_dependencies.description:
Edges the function traverses. Same role as
`property_dependencies` but for relationship presence.

name.description:
Short, human-readable name. Not required to be a valid
identifier — the compilation step that lowers a function to
a source dialect produces a mangled name from the id.

property_dependencies.description:
Properties the function reads. Used for cache-invalidation
fan-out — when any listed property changes, memoized results
for this function are dropped.

purity.description:
Whether the planner may memoize calls with equal arguments.
`Impure` functions (today / now / random) never get cached.

FunctionExpression.description:
Dialect-free function body.

Each variant carries the shape the compiler needs to emit the
appropriate source dialect. `SqlExpr` and `CypherExpr` are
verbatim — the author's expression must already be valid for the
target. `BuiltIn` names a function the platform implements
itself (e.g. `now`, `coalesce`). `Udf` points at a Wasm binary or
other externally-built artifact; the content of the binary is
stored out-of-band.

FunctionPurity.description: Purity tag that drives memoization / plan stability.

oneOf.description:
Reciprocal Rank Fusion. For each result candidate, its
fused score is `sum_over_sources(1.0 / (k + rank))`
where `k` is the smoothing constant (default 60 per
the original paper).

k.description:
Smoothing constant. Higher values flatten the
per-source weight; lower values let the top-k
candidates dominate.

oneOf.description:
Weighted sum of per-source scores. Reserved for v2 —
the v1 routes always pick `ReciprocalRankFusion`.
Lands here in the type space so the dispatcher's
match doesn't need a future-shape rewrite.

FusionStrategy.description:
Per-side score-fusion strategy. `ReciprocalRankFusion` is
the v1 default — the most well-studied + stable hybrid
fusion method (Cormack et al. 2009); weighted-sum is a
future option once the platform's cost model has the data
to pick weights informed by per-workspace retrieval
quality stats.

GateId.description:
Stable identifier for a single gate the operator must satisfy
before invoking the design action. New variants are additive —
the FE i18n catalogue keys gate copy by `GateId`.
